title: Lifecycle Composer: Per-route retention, residency, and evidence export orchestrator for inference artifacts
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Define and deliver a policy-driven lifecycle orchestrator that lets customers express per-route retention and residency for prompts, responses, request logs and metrics, and automates evidence/export generation for audits. This ticket covers the product requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout strategy, and coordination with runtime and engineering to implement enforcement hooks, backfill/migration tooling, and Console/UI controls.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can set per-route TTL and residency (region/tenant) defaults in Console and via API
Retention rules apply to four artifact classes: prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics
Automated evidence packages (signed bundles) can be generated on-demand and on-schedule containing provenance metadata and cryptographic hashes
System respects legal hold: artifacts marked for hold are excluded from eviction workflows
Cross-region replication and deletion follow residency constraints and produce audit events visible in Console
Retention changes are non-destructive by default and include a simulator/preview before commit
technical_notes: Integrate with runtime's retention hooks (ENG-51234) to surface per-request metadata for eviction decisions
Define a compact retention DSL that composes route, tenant, and session-level rules and resolves precedence deterministically
Provide a migration/backfill path that creates a snapshot and incremental eviction plan to avoid throttling serving clusters
Evidence export format: ZIP with manifest.json (SHA-256 hashes), signed by KMS key; include request IDs, timestamps, model version, and route policy resolution log
Export jobs should be sharded and rate-limited to avoid impacting live inference; use dedicated export workers
Implement sampling hooks for high-volume routes: configurable sample rate with deterministic hashing to ensure reproducible samples for audits
ux_notes: Console: 'Lifecycle Composer' page to create policies, preview effective TTLs for example requests, and simulate evictions
Per-route quick actions: set default TTL, toggle residency constraint, enable evidence snapshotting
Evidence export UI: schedule, one-off export, and download link with signed manifest and chain-of-custody timeline
Warnings and indicators for routes that violate residency requirements (e.g., route allows cross-region caching)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): enable for Redwood-managed tenants in staging; validate eviction correctness and export integrity
Phase 2 (beta): expose Console controls to selected customers, provide migration tool and support playbook
Phase 3 (GA): global rollout with API docs, SDK helpers, and retention simulator; provide published SLA for export latency
Post-GA: telemetry-based recommendations in Redwood Optimize for TTL suggestions and cost impact estimates
